坐姿將琴靠於肩上或置於身前。將樂器穩定持於身前。左手負責按弦或改變有效弦長以控制: Sitting, rest the instrument on the shoulder or hold it in front of the body. Hold the instrument steady in front of you. The left hand stops the strings or changes the vibrating length to control the pitch, and the right hand makes the strings sound. On a chordophone the principle is that the vibration of the string is amplified through the soundbox. Pluck the strings with a fingertip or a plectrum, watching the angle and the force of contact.

塔格爾哈帕弓琴可見於現代民俗音樂，愛沙尼亞新民俗（nu-folk）雙人組合 Pu: The tagelharpa is found in modern folk music: the Estonian nu-folk duo Puuluup play the tagelharpa with live looping. Historically it appeared in the Estonian-Swedish areas and in western Estonia, especially among the Estonian Swedish community. Others of the bowed-lyre family are the jouhikko in Finland and the crwth in Wales; the sources list no particular composers or pieces.
塔格爾哈帕弓琴為北歐兩至四弦弓奏里拉。其是否曾於斯堪地納維亞普遍流行仍有疑問。歷: The tagelharpa is a two- to four-stringed bowed lyre of northern Europe. Whether it was ever widespread in Scandinavia is still in doubt. Historically it appears in the Estonian-Swedish areas and in western Estonia, and it may have been brought by the Estonian Swedes who moved in from the Swedish-speaking parts of Finland around the tenth century; later Swedish immigrants were unfamiliar with it or did not use it. The earliest mention of a harp or lyre in Nordic literature is in the Völuspá, but that is not a bowed instrument. Images of a lyre played in a snake pit and a fourteenth-century stone carving at Trondheim Cathedral have also been tentatively read as related instruments. The bowed lyre survives as the jouhikko in Finland and as the hiiu kannel in Estonia.
塔格爾哈帕弓琴音色溫潤而富有古樸韻味，帶有明亮的穿透力與悠遠的歷史質感。其音域為: The tagelharpa's timbre is warm and full of an old-fashioned flavour, with a bright penetration and a distant sense of history. Its range lies in the upper middle register, and the tone is clear without being harsh. With only two to four strings, each string has its own full quality and a deep resonance. The resonance produced inside the body gives the tone a warm wooden quality, like a medieval harp but more desolate. Changes in bow pressure produce fine gradations of tone, from light and drifting to deep and powerful. Against the bright sharpness of the modern violin, the tagelharpa is more inward and mysterious; against a folk bagpipe its tone is softer and more intimate. The sound of this old instrument seems to come from the pale land and sky of the north, with a strong regional character and a sense of history.
塔格爾哈帕（Tagelharpa）是北歐的兩至四弦拉奏里拉琴，屬弦鳴樂器，霍恩博: The tagelharpa is a two- to four-stringed bowed lyre of northern Europe, a chordophone, Hornbostel–Sachs 321.22-71. Traditionally it is made by hollowing out a single piece of wood and gluing on a soundboard, and it is played with a bow. Historically it is found in the Estonian Swedish areas and in western Estonia, played especially by Estonian Swedes; today it is occasionally used in folk music, for example by an Estonian duo who play it with live looping.
琴身傳統由單一木塊挖空，上貼音板；現代仍多以實木製作，也有採古典製琴學分件組裝，: The body is traditionally hollowed from a single block of wood with a soundboard glued on; today it is still mostly made of solid wood, and some makers use the classical luthier's method of separate parts, including the reinforcement, the hoop, the counter-hoop, the figured bottom and the blocks. The strings are traditionally of horsehair, and the sound is produced as on any chordophone. The sources do not state the materials of the bow, the fingerboard, the pegs and the remaining parts.
